bib.title: Mixture-of-Transformers: A Sparse and Scalable Architecture for Multi-Modal Foundation Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Mixture-of-Transformers: A Sparse and Scalable Architecture for Multi-Modal Foundation Models. Weixin Liang, Lili Yu, Liang Luo, Srinivasan Iyer, Ning Dong, Chunting Zhou, Gargi Ghosh, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Luke Zettlemoyer, Xi Victoria Lin (Stanford, AI at Meta). Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 04/2025 (arXiv 2411.04996v2, May 2025).

COVERAGE: Pages 1-48 of 48 were extracted. About 149k chars read in full, covering the abstract, all sections (1-8), Appendices A-B and the Appendix C figure captions. References were skimmed. Figure bodies (plots, images) were not viewed, only their captions and axis text. Page numbers below are approximate, taken from the contents list. The extraction is noisy: tables and plot labels are fragmented, but the prose is clean.

CLAIMS
1. MoT matches a 7B dense baseline in the Chameleon setting (text+image, both autoregressive) with 55.8% of the FLOPs.
 number: 55.8% of FLOPs (44.2% reduction); 45.5% of steps on global training loss; 34.8% on image loss.
 setup: 7B, FLOPs-controlled, trained from scratch, 120k steps, 0.377T tokens, roughly equal text and image tokens. Compared on held-out Obelisc, COCO, Flickr and Shutterstock validation losses.
 quote: "MoT at 55.8% training steps achieves comparable or lower validation losses than dense model's final loss, indicating 44.2% reduction in required training FLOPs." Also: "MoT particularly effective for image modality, requiring 34.8% of dense model's training steps to match final loss."
 where: Fig 5, p.11; sec 3.2.2, p.13-14

2. Adding speech as a third modality, MoT reaches dense speech quality with 37.2% of the FLOPs.
 number: 37.2% of FLOPs on speech validation; 22.9% of steps on speech training loss; 15.1%-33.6% of steps across 443M/880M/1.5B.
 setup: 7B Chameleon+Speech. Speech is discrete semantic tokens (DinoSR variant, vocab 500, 25Hz). Speech data is mixed with text+image data at 1:6.
 quote: "MoT reaches baseline speech performance in 37.2% of the FLOPs (f)." Also: "MoT required only 15.1% to 33.6% of the dense model's training steps to match speech training loss across all scales."
 where: Fig 8, Fig 9, sec 3.3, p.15-18

3. In the Transfusion setting (text autoregressive, image diffusion), a 760M MoT beats a 1.4B dense model at half the FLOPs.
 number: CLIP 0.214 vs 0.206; FID 21.145 vs 24.688; CIDEr 0.320 vs 0.286.
 setup: Transfusion, 0.5T tokens (text:image 1:1), 250k steps, 256x256 images, 380M licensed Shutterstock images, FLOPs-controlled. No classifier-free guidance unless noted.
 quote: "The 760M MoT model, using half the training/inference FLOPs of the 1.4B dense baseline (Transfusion), consistently outperforms the dense model across metrics: CLIP score (0.214 vs 0.206, higher is better), FID score (21.145 vs 24.688, lower is better), CIDEr score for image captioning (0.320 vs 0.286, higher is better)"
 where: Fig 10-11, sec 3.4.2, p.20-22

4. A 7B Transfusion MoT matches the dense image loss in about 30% of the steps and gets better FID and captioning.
 number: 30% of steps; COCO-30k FID 8.14 vs 9.22; CIDEr 40.6 vs 31.5.
 setup: the 9.22 FID is a dense model trained on 1T tokens with richer data, not a matched run. FID is at guidance level 1.6. CIDEr is the final score.
 quote: "MoT achieves equivalent image pre-training loss to the dense model in only 30% of the training steps." Also: "we compute the COCO-30k FID at a guidance level of 1.6 and obtain a score of 8.14. In contrast, a dense model trained on 1T tokens with richer data achieves a COCO-30k FID of 9.22". Also: "achieving a final score of 40.6 versus 31.5."
 where: sec 3.4.2, p.21

5. Wall-clock gains are real but measured on one cluster only.
 number: 47.2% of dense time for image loss, 75.6% for text. MoE-4x shows a 1.7x slowdown on image.
 setup: Chameleon 7B, 256 A100 GPUs, AWS p4de.24xlarge, FSDP full shard, PyTorch 2 compile.
 quote: "MoT matches the dense model's image training loss in 47.2% of the total GPU training time" and "MoE-4x exhibits no speed advantage in the text modality (Figure 19d) and even results in a 1.7x slowdown in the image modality compared to the dense model"
 where: sec 6.2.2, Fig 19, p.32-34

6. MoT's gain grows with GPU count, from a pilot study.
 number: image 42.1% to 21.6% of steps; text 75.7% to 50.9% (16 to 256 GPUs).
 setup: Chameleon 443M. Global batch and tokens scale with GPU count at constant steps.
 quote: "the percentage of training steps required for MoT to match the dense model decreases from 42.1% (16 GPUs) to 21.6% (256 GPUs). For text, this percentage decreases from 75.7% to 50.9%."
 where: sec 6.2.1, Fig 18, p.32

7. MoT beats MoE-4x, which has more total parameters. MoE-4x gains on image shrink with scale and vanish at 7B.
 number: none (qualitative). Example step ratios, 7B image: MoT s=0.348, MoE-4x s=1.012, where s above 1 means no speedup.
 setup: MoE-4x uses Expert Choice routing, FLOPs-matched. Chameleon 37M to 7B.
 quote: "MoE-4x exhibits diminishing gains in image modality as scale increases, with advantages disappearing at 7B." In the speech setting MoE-4x showed "improvements in training loss but unstable generalization in validation, particularly for speech".
 where: Fig 6, sec 3.2.3, 3.3.3, p.12-17

8. Ablation: untying the FFN gives the biggest gain. Attention QKV untying adds more, and LayerNorm untying adds nothing.
 number: approx 33.3% extra FLOPs saving on image and 10% on text from adding attention untying on top of FFN untying (Obelisc).
 setup: 880M Chameleon, FLOPs-matched to dense.
 quote: "this leads to approximately 33.3% FLOPs saving for the image modailty and 10% FLOPs saving for the text modality compared to only performing untying in the feedforward module." Also: "untying the LayerNorm parameters on top of feedforward and attention untying has a negligible impact"
 where: sec 3.5, Fig 14, p.25-26

9. Leave-one-out: merging modalities into one tower hurts, and the effects are not symmetric.
 number: none.
 setup: 443M Chameleon+Speech, FLOPs-matched.
 quote: "Combining modalities consistently degraded performance, as evidenced by higher training and validation losses across configurations." Also: "This differential impact suggests non-reciprocal modality competition effects."
 where: sec 4, Fig 15, p.26-27

10. Gains across scales in Transfusion (MoT vs dense).
 number: FID 21.58 vs 27.42 (163M), 15.75 vs 25.58 (760M), 15.85 vs 19.32 (1.4B). MoT reaches dense image loss in 17.5%-26.4% of steps.
 quote: "FID scores showed substantial improvements for MoT over dense models: 21.58 vs 27.42 (163M), 15.75 vs 25.58 (760M), and 15.85 vs 19.32 (1.4B)."
 where: sec 3.4.3, Fig 12, p.22-23

11. The text gain is small or absent in Transfusion. In Chameleon, MoT needed 54.6%-66.2% of steps for text.
 quote: "In Transfusion, the text performance improvement was marginal to none (see Appendix 26)."
 setup: authors' hypotheses are that the separate objectives already decouple text, that text is less compute-intensive, and that the gains favor heavy modalities.
 where: sec 3.4.2, p.21-22

12. Parameter growth is lower than MoE (Parameters-per-FLOP argument).
 number: MoE adds more than 3(E-1)D^2 parameters per layer. MoT adds 7(K-1)D^2 per layer.
 setup: SwiGLU FFN with 3D^2 parameters, attention KQVO with 4D^2; E experts, K modalities.
 quote: "MoT incurs an added parameter count of (K-1)x(|ATTN|+|FFN|) = 7(K-1)D^2."
 where: sec 6.1, p.31

13. MoT hybridizes with MoE: putting MoE-4x in the text FFN improves text further without hurting image. This is a preliminary proof of concept.
 number: none beyond step ratios, for example text s=0.431 at Chameleon 373M.
 where: sec 5, Fig 16-17, p.28-30

14. Motivation: dense models show modality clustering in feature space (PCA, 7B Chameleon+Speech dense). Chameleon used 9.2T tokens to match LLaMA2, which used 2T.
 quote: "Chameleon (Chameleon Team, 2024) is trained on 9.2 trillion training tokens (including image tokens) to match LLaMA2 (Touvron et al., 2023b), which is trained on 2 trillion training tokens for text performance."
 where: sec 1 p.4, Fig 2 and Fig 23

METHOD (short): Each token is routed by a fixed modality tag, with no learned router. Every non-embedding weight is per modality: FFN, Q/K/V/O projections, and both LayerNorms. Attention is global self-attention over the whole interleaved sequence. FLOPs and active parameters equal the dense model. Equation 2: "a = GlobalAttn(x,{theta_attn^m}), h_i = x_i + LayerNorm_attn^{m_i}(a_i), output_i = h_i + LayerNorm_ffn^{m_i}(FFN(h_i, theta_ffn^{m_i}))".

LIMITS
- The authors say they are "focus[ing] on evaluating the relative performance ... rather than conducting a scaling law study".
- Most "FLOPs saved" figures are step-matching on training or validation loss, not downstream accuracy. Downstream metrics (FID, CLIP, CIDEr) appear only in the Transfusion setting.
- MoE-4x uses Expert Choice routing evaluated with the same routing. The authors concede this may overestimate MoE through future-token leakage, or underestimate it under distribution shift. Caption results for MoE-4x were excluded.
- Wall-clock and horizontal-scaling results are tied to one AWS A100 setup: "Further investigation is needed to generalize these findings".
- MoT overheads (CPU-GPU sync for grouping tokens, sequential per-modality processing, load imbalance) were not on the critical path in their setup. Group GEMM and Megablocks fixes are left as future work.
- The Transfusion text gain is small or absent. The 7B image-quality comparison uses a 1T-token dense model with richer data, so it is not matched.
- Trained on only 0.5T tokens, which is much less than other state-of-the-art image generators. Fine-tuning evidence is qualitative: samples are shown and some hard prompts fail for both models.
- LayerNorm untying was tested only in combination with FFN and attention untying. Combining with MoE is a preliminary result only.
- The inference section gives deployment ideas (dynamic batching, padding to one batched GEMM), with no measured inference numbers.
- Only three modalities were tried: text, image and speech. The text/image vocabularies and the tokenizers are as in Chameleon and Transfusion.

BUILDS ON
- Chameleon Team 2024: early-fusion, discrete image tokens, data.
- Zhou et al. 2024 (Transfusion): continuous image tokens with a diffusion loss.
- Nguyen et al. 2024 (SpiRit-LM): speech data.
- Liu et al. 2024a (DinoSR variant): speech tokenizer.
- Gafni et al. 2022: image tokenizer.
- Lin et al. 2024: modality-specific FFNs (also named as the FFN-only untying baseline).
- Bao et al. 2022 (VLMo), Wang et al. 2022, Shen et al. 2023: modality-aware MoE.
- Wang et al. 2023 (CogVLM), He et al. 2024: modality-specific modules on an LLM backbone.
- Playground v3 (Liu et al. 2024b): concurrent.
- Zhou et al. 2022: Expert Choice routing, used for the MoE baseline.
- Jacobs 1991, Shazeer 2017, Fedus 2022: MoE.
- Alayrac et al. 2022 (Flamingo): cross-attention alternative.
- Esser et al. 2024 (SD3): diffusion validation loss as predictor.

CODE: Algorithm 1 (sec 2.2, p.9) is pseudocode. The key lines are: group tokens by modality, apply modality-specific Q/K/V projections, restore sequence order, run global self-attention, apply modality-specific output projection with LayerNorm, then modality-specific FFN with LayerNorm. The playbook repo is https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mixture-of-Transformers.

FIGURES (captions only; bodies not viewed)
- Fig 1 and Fig 3 (p.4, p.8): MoT architecture, with modality-specific weights, then global attention.
- Fig 2 (p.7): PCA of the dense model's features, clustered by modality. This is the motivation.
- Fig 5 (p.11): the 7B Chameleon headline, with loss curves and step matching.
- Fig 6 (p.12): step matching across 37M to 7B, MoT vs MoE-2x/3x/4x. The s values summarize the speedup.
- Fig 8 and Fig 9 (p.16, p.18): speech results.
- Fig 11 (p.22): 760M MoT vs 1.4B dense on FID, CLIP and CIDEr.
- Fig 14 (p.25): untying ablation.
- Fig 15 (p.26): leave-one-out.
- Fig 18 (p.33): GPU-count scaling.
- Fig 19 (p.34): wall-clock, MoT vs MoE-4x.
- Fig 13, 20-22: sample images, qualitative.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table and figure text is fragmented, and a few typos came from the extraction ("2.10N" in Table 4; "five different sizes" is followed by four listed). Step-match "s" values are ratios read from plot labels. The abstract's "one third of the FLOPs" for 7B Transfusion image corresponds to the body's "30% of steps" and "less than one third of the FLOPs" (sec 1). The Fig 5 caption and section 3.2.2 give 45.5% (steps on global loss) and 55.8% (FLOPs on validation), which are different metrics. Page numbers are inferred.
